title: Convolutional Networks: Filters, Stride, Padding and Pooling
summary: How convolutional layers exploit locality and weight sharing: multi-channel filters, the cross-correlation convention, the output-size formula for stride and padding, im2col for speed, and max-pooling with its argmax-routing gradient.
takeaways: A filter spans all input channels. F filters of shape (C, KH, KW) produce F output channels.
Deep-learning 'convolution' is cross-correlation. The kernel isn't flipped, because the weights are learned anyway.
H_out = ⌊(H + 2p − K)/s⌋ + 1. Get the floor right and every layer's shape follows.
Max-pool backward routes each gradient to its window's argmax, accumulating when windows overlap.

steps.label: Pad
steps.detail: Add p zeros around H and W so edge pixels can sit under the kernel's center.

steps.label: Gather patches
steps.detail: im2col: one row of C·KH·KW values per output position, stepping by the stride.

steps.label: Multiply
steps.detail: cols @ w.reshape(F, −1).T + b computes every filter at every position at once.

steps.label: Pool
steps.detail: Max over k×k windows to downsample, then pass the result to the next layer.

terms.definition: Sliding a kernel over the input and taking dot products without flipping it, which is what Conv2d computes.
The input region that one output value depends on.
How many pixels the window moves between output positions.
A border of zeros added around the input to control the output size.
Unrolling input patches into matrix rows so convolution becomes a single matrix multiply.
Replacing each window with its maximum. It has no parameters and routes gradients to the argmax.
